evidence: Documents tab lists 19 documents each tagged with a module (API, AUTH, Data Layer, UI Components, Core System) and module filter buttons (All/API/AUTH/DATA/UI/CORE) let users browse by module.

Opening "REST API Design Guidelines" shows title (h1), description, Content Sections (REST Principles, Endpoint Naming Conventions, Pagination & Filtering) and a Related Documents list (API Versioning Strategy, Error Handling Standards, HTTP Methods Guide, Rate Limiting).

Clicking "API Versioning Strategy" link inside the expanded REST Principles section navigated the document viewer to the API Versioning Strategy document (heading, sections, related docs updated accordingly).
Clicking the "Versioning Approaches" section header collapsed it: the paragraph and its formerly-clickable link disappeared/became non-interactive.
Clicking the collapsed "Versioning Approaches" header again re-expanded it, restoring the paragraph text and re-enabling the "REST API Guidelines" link (cursor=pointer).

In the Knowledge Graph tab, clicking a node (e.g. "REST API Design Guidelines") sets it as the selected document and auto-expands its first content section (verified doc/section state changed after the click), and module legend/nodes are interactive (cursor=pointer).

Knowledge Graph tab renders an SVG containing all 19 document nodes as labeled, color-coded (by module) elements plus a module legend, zoom controls, and a zoom percentage indicator (100%), giving a full view of the graph.
Header navigation exposes exactly three tabs: "Documents", "Knowledge Graph", and "Favorites", each switching the main content area accordingly.

Collapsed the "REST Principles" section on Documents tab, then switched to Favorites tab and back — section remained collapsed. Separately, zoomed Knowledge Graph to 140%, switched to Favorites tab and back to Knowledge Graph — zoom level remained 140%.

Knowledge Graph tab shows an interactive node-link diagram connecting all documents, color-coded by module with a legend, pan/zoom controls, and clickable nodes that navigate to documents — matches the dynamic knowledge graph visualization requirement.
Programmatic check of /src/data/documents.ts: for every document object, its relatedDocuments array does not contain its own id (0 self-references found across all documents).

All 19 document titles appear as graph nodes, each colored per its module (API/Authentication/Data Layer/UI Components/Core System) matching the module legend, confirming the graph corresponds to the real documents/modules dataset.

Source inspection of DocumentViewer.tsx and KnowledgeGraph.tsx shows handleRelatedDocClick/handleNodeClick both call getDocumentById(id) and, if the target document doesn't exist, call showToast('...not found','error') and return without navigating or throwing — the app is not broken by invalid links. All real related-document ids in documents.ts resolve to existing documents, so this guard is the only path for invalid ids.

Each content section header shows a chevron icon that changes and toggles visibility of the paragraph/content beneath it; collapsed sections hide their paragraph and disable their link (no cursor=pointer) while expanded sections show the paragraph and an active link (cursor=pointer), giving a clear visual state indicator.

Clicked the "REST API Design Guidelines" node in the Knowledge Graph; switching to the Documents tab afterward showed that document selected/open as the active document view, confirming the node click navigated to that document.

Clicked "Add to favorites" on Accessibility Standards and Data Migrations; the Favorites tab label updated in real time to "Favorites 2" and both cards switched to "Remove from favorites". Filtering by module "UI" still showed Accessibility Standards marked as favorite; after resetting filter and sorting by "Last Updated", both documents remained marked "Remove from favorites" and the count stayed at 2, confirming favorite markers survive filtering/sorting and are tracked with a live count (zustand persist middleware also persists favorites to localStorage under 'tech-docs-storage').
